en: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Shall I not inform you concerning the Dajjal a narration that no prophet ever narrated to his people? Indeed, he is one-eyed, and he will bring with him the likeness of Paradise and the Fire; that which he says is Paradise is the Fire. And indeed, I have warned you of him just as Nuh warned his people of him.'

'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Hujr's; Ishaq said: 'informed us', and Ibn Hujr said: 'narrated to us'—Jarir narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: Hudhayfah and Abu Mas'ud met together, and Hudhayfah said: 'I certainly know what is with the Dajjal better than he does. With him is a river of water and a river of fire; as for that which you see as fire, it is water, and as for that which you see as water, it is fire. So whoever among you reaches that and wants water, let him drink from that which he sees as fire, for he will find it to be water.' Abu Mas'ud said: 'This is how I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying.'

'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Shu'ayb ibn Safwan narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amr Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: I went with him to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and 'Uqbah said to him: 'Narrate to me what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning the Dajjal.' He said: 'The Dajjal will emerge, and with him will be water and fire. As for what people see as water, it is burning fire; and as for what people see as fire, it is cool, sweet water. So whoever among you reaches that, let him plunge into what he sees as fire, for it is sweet, wholesome water.' 'Uqbah said: 'And I have heard it as well, confirming Hudhayfah.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'I know what is with the Dajjal better than he does. With him are two flowing rivers: one of them, to the sight of the eye, is white water, and the other, to the sight of the eye, is blazing fire. So if anyone encounters him, let him go to the river that he sees as fire, close his eyes, then lower his head and drink from it, for it is cool water. And indeed, the Dajjal has a wiped-out eye over which is a thick piece of flesh; written between his eyes is Kafir, which every believer will read, whether literate or illiterate.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: 'informed us', and the other two said: 'narrated to us'—Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal is blind in the left eye, with abundant hair. With him is a paradise and a fire; so his fire is a paradise and his paradise is a fire.'

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us [H]; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us—and the wording is his: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said concerning the Dajjal: 'Indeed, with him are water and fire; his fire is cool water and his water is fire, so do not perish!' Abu Mas'ud said: 'And I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Affan narrated to us: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal has a wiped-out eye; written between his eyes is Kafir'—then he spelled it out: K-F-R—'which every Muslim can read.'

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—both saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal has written between his eyes: K-F-R, meaning Kafir.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There has been no prophet except that he warned his nation of the one-eyed liar. Behold, he is one-eyed, whereas your Lord is not one-eyed, and written between his eyes is: K-F-R.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Husayn—meaning Ibn Hasan ibn Yasar—narrated to us: Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: Nafi' used to say: 'Ibn Sayyad.' He said: Ibn 'Umar said: I met him twice. He said: I met him and said to one of them: 'Do you say that he is he?' He said: 'No, by Allah.' He said: I said: 'You lied to me! By Allah, some of you informed me that he will not die until he becomes the one with the most wealth and children among you, and so he is today, according to what they claim.' He said: We talked, then I departed from him. He said: Then I met him on another occasion, and his eye was swollen. He said: I said: 'When did your eye do what I see?' He said: 'I do not know.' He said: I said: 'You do not know, and yet it is in your head?' He said: 'If Allah wills, He could create it in this staff of yours!' He said: Then he snorted with the loudest snorting of a donkey I had ever heard. He said: Some of my companions claimed that I struck him with a staff I had with me until it broke, but as for me, by Allah, I was not conscious of that. He said: And he came until he entered upon the Mother of the Believers and narrated it to her. She said: 'What do you want with him? Did you not know that he said: "Indeed, the first thing that unleashes him upon the people is anger that enrages him"?'

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', who said: Ibn 'Umar met Ibn Sa'id in one of the alleys of Medina and said something to him that angered him, so he swelled up until he filled the entire alleyway. Ibn 'Umar then entered upon Hafsah, who had already heard of it, and she said to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you! What did you want with Ibn Sa'id? Did you not know that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "He will only emerge out of anger that enrages him"?'

And 'Abd ibn Humayd and Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, both from 'Abd ar-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed by Ibn Sayyad along with a group of his companions among whom was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, while he was playing with the boys near the fortress of Banu Maghalah, and he was a young boy... with the meaning of the hadith of Yunus and Salih, except that 'Abd ibn Humayd did not mention the hadith of Ibn 'Umar regarding the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) going with Ubayy ibn Ka'b to the date palms.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Ya'qub—and he is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Salim ibn 'Abdullah informed me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar informed him that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab set out with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), accompanied by a group of his companions among whom was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, until he found Ibn Sayyad as a boy approaching puberty playing with the boys near the fortress of Banu Mu'awiyah... and he conveyed the hadith like the hadith of Yunus up to the end of the hadith of 'Umar ibn Thabit. And in the hadith from Ya'qub he said: Ubayy said—meaning regarding his saying 'If she had left him alone, he would have made it clear'—he said: 'If his mother had left him alone, his case would have become clear.'
